title: Vegas Part 03
summary: Episode 115 closes the Las Vegas hotel-room sequence. It begins with a corrupted half-minute followed by an explicit off-air boundary, then moves through gambling risk, an escort guest's work history, repeated publication and privacy issues, an adult/minor sexual history that requires child-abuse framing, incorrect client-count arithmetic, racial exclusions and other offensive ideas, increasing intoxication, sexualized pressure toward a hotel worker, direct no/fisting corrections, unsafe lubricant and body-food practices, and a late admission that internal food insertion occurred without the guest's knowledge. The audit preserves every idea and contradiction, corrects only context-supported words, and keeps factual, consent, health and public-discovery judgments outside the dialogue.
source_notes: The raw file contains 3,443 segments and approximately 20,415 words; the clean file contains 3,368 segments and approximately 20,450 words across 5,971.66 seconds.

The cleaner reports seventy-five changes. Sixty-two occur in the opening 29.96 seconds, where a 20.7778 compression ratio and repeated `Your` tokens indicate hallucination; the current twelve indistinct markers should become one bounded marker after immutable-audio regeneration. The other thirteen removals are empty zero-duration artifacts.

Accept Humaniplex, Asa Akira, Kaylani Lei, RealDoll, Jenna Jameson, pole tricks, penile piercings, black guys and Larry Flynt only where local context supports them. Reject a global deletion of `the` before Bellagio and leave other garbled names uncertain pending audio verification.
The first intelligible line says the subject should be discussed off air, followed by checks that nothing was said. That boundary survives the general warning that recording is active.

The guest describes sex at twelve with a nineteen-year-old and another older-person encounter at thirteen. These are child sexual abuse/exploitation; retrospective love, pursuit or defense cannot create legal consent. Names, relatives, street, social account, wife and children remain outside public discovery.

The cast's count math is wrong: five appointments per week is about 260 per year, and about 2,600 over ten years before repeat clients—not 420 per year or 4,200 unique men. The claimed two-million-dollar gross remains speculative.
The guest's racial client exclusions and the cast's racial stereotypes remain literal ideas. They are not rewritten or censored, but neither are they promoted as neutral demographic facts.
At roughly 1:03:25 the cast says the guest is too drunk/wasted and cuts off alcohol. That is material capacity evidence for later body-food and sexual acts.

A hotel room-service worker is questioned about identity and employment, offered money, told sexualized participation is part of the job, and repeatedly tries to leave. Service, customer pressure, a tip or payment are not consent; identifying details remain restricted.
The guest directly says a prior statement was not an invitation, and another speaker says no does not permit fisting. Porn performance, pain or prior acts do not grant real-life consent.

Baby oil can degrade latex condoms. Internal food insertion can cause irritation, infection or a retained foreign body. The guest later says she did not know gummy bears had been inserted and one remained lost.

The spoken historical review-site identifier, current prices, travel, schedules, client locations, worker identity, hotel access, private partners and family remain outside public discovery. The underlying ideas remain in the transcript.
The speakers explicitly say they are not filming. Audio recording awareness cannot be converted into video permission.
Five coarse identity windows and zero diarized turns do not pass held-out multispeaker validation. Named dialogue remains withheld.
speaker_policy: The recording names recurring cast, a guest and public people, but only five coarse embeddings and zero diarized turns exist. These do not pass independently held-out multispeaker validation. Named dialogue remains withheld.
